title: GE Oven F2 Error Code: How to Fix an Overheating Fault
metaDescription: GE oven flashing F2 or F2 E0 mid-bake? It's an overheat/temperature-sensor fault. Here's how to check the sensor and the door, and reset it safely.
symptom: The oven beeps, displays "F2" (or "F2 E0"), and shuts off heat mid-cycle — sometimes during self-clean.

steps.heading: Let the oven cool completely
steps.body: F2 means the control board detected the oven exceeding its safe temperature range (often triggered during self-clean). Cancel the cycle at the breaker if it won't respond, and let the oven cool fully — at least an hour — before touching anything inside.

steps.heading: Locate the temperature sensor
steps.body: It's the small metal probe (a slim rod, not a screw) mounted on the back or side wall of the oven cavity, separate from any control knob. It should hang free, not touch the oven walls or racks.

steps.heading: Check for contact with the oven wall or a rack
steps.body: If the sensor probe is bent and touching the cavity wall, it will read inaccurately and can trigger F2. Gently bend it back to hang about 1/2 inch clear of the wall — do this only when the oven is cool.

steps.heading: Test the sensor's resistance
steps.body: With the oven unplugged, unclip the sensor's wire connector at the back of the oven and check its resistance with a multimeter. At room temperature it should read close to the spec in your model's manual (often near 1,080 ohms for GE ovens). A reading far off spec, or no continuity at all, means the sensor has failed.

steps.heading: Replace the sensor if it's out of spec
steps.body: The sensor typically unscrews from inside the cavity and unplugs from a connector at the back — no wiring to cut. Replacements are inexpensive and this is a beginner-friendly swap once the oven is unplugged and cool.

whenToCallAPro: If the sensor tests within spec and isn't touching the cavity wall, but F2 keeps returning — especially if it happens outside of self-clean — the issue is likely the control board itself (a more expensive part) and is worth a professional diagnosis before buying one on a guess.
safetyWarnings: Never open a hot oven door to work inside — wait for a full cool-down, especially after a self-clean cycle which can exceed 800°F.
Unplug the oven (or shut off its breaker) before removing any back panel or touching wiring — ovens run on a 240V circuit.
If F2 appeared during self-clean, don't run self-clean again until the cause is fixed — repeated overheat faults are a fire-risk signal, not a glitch to ignore.
